title: The Wild Crown Anew
premise: Yara Nystrom, youngest keeper of the Ledger of the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers the guild's accounts hide a debt older than any kingdom: a bargain that bound a living king to a crown-entity called the Verdant Wearer, which feeds on oaths of loyalty. When a feral child arrives speaking the pre-kingdom tongue, Yara realizes the boy is the original oath made flesh — and the only key to unbinding it. Betrayed by his own guildmaster, who has been trading years of members' lives to keep the crown fed, Yara must choose between the found family that raised him and the truth that will destroy them. In the end he rewrites the ledger itself, unbinding the king at the cost of the guild's magic and his own name from every memory but the child's.
about_author: Noor Dunmore is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing merchant ledgers in coastal trading towns before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about paperwork, promises, and the people caught between them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He balances the guild's impossible ledgers — bottled storms, borrowed shadows — while hiding that entries in his own hand have begun vanishing. A routine delivery reveals a page burned with a royal seal. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath competence; Yara senses the guild is keeping secrets even from its own.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the night of the frost-moon, a mud-caked boy appears at the guild door speaking a language no member recognizes — except the ledgers do, matching it glyph for glyph in the oldest volume. The guildmaster, Sable Vane, orders the boy locked away. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into unease as Yara realizes the guild expected this arrival.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Remember
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with an interlude in the boy Tam's fragmented perspective. Translating through the ledgers, Yara learns Tam is not a child but an oath given form — the first promise ever sworn to the crown. Emotional beat: tenderness toward Tam mixed with horror at what the guild has been feeding.

chapters.title: The King Who Waits
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, dreamlike. Tam remembers being sworn: a young king binding himself to the Verdant Wearer to end a famine, each renewal costing him memories. Present-day courtiers arrive at the guild seeking 'the asset.' Emotional beat: grief and compassion — the king is both victim and jailer of himself.

chapters.title: Entries in Red Ink
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Auditing hidden pages, Yara finds the guild's true trade: decades of members' lifespans sold to the crown to sustain the Wearer, including his late mentor's. Confronting Sable, he is offered partnership and silence. Emotional beat: betrayal; loyalty to the guild wars with the truth in his hands.

chapters.title: The Road to Thornhold
chapters.summary: Alternating Yara and Tam POV. Fleeing with Tam, Yara joins two exiled guild members — brash ferrywoman Odile and disgraced oath-scribe Merrick — forming a fragile found family on the road to the capital. Pursuers close in. Emotional beat: warmth and belonging hard-won, shadowed by the knowledge that someone keeps selling them out.

chapters.title: The Price Already Paid
chapters.summary: Merrick's POV. Ambushed at a border shrine, the group learns Merrick has been reporting to Sable to buy back his stolen years. Odile is gravely wounded covering their escape. Emotional beat: rage and forgiveness tangled; Yara chooses mercy over vengeance, deepening the family bond even as trust fractures.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Crown
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Infiltrating Thornhold, they find the king: half-consumed, lucid only in fragments, begging to be freed yet terrified of what the Wearer becomes without him. The entity offers Yara anything — his mentor restored, the guild saved — if he leaves Tam. Emotional beat: temptation at its most personal.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Tam and Yara's alternating POV. Climax. Before the assembled court, Yara reads the original oath aloud and begins rewriting it in the pre-kingdom tongue while Tam willingly dissolves back into words. Sable arrives to stop him; the guild's loyalists must finally choose. The king is unbound; the Wearer, starved of false loyalty, unravels. Emotional beat: sacrifice, courage, heartbreak as Tam fades smiling.

chapters.title: The Wild Crown Anew
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue-like. The guild's magic is gone, its debts settled; Sable faces judgment, and the freed king abdicates, crowning the land itself wild again. Yara's name survives only in Tam's last written word — carved on the guild door. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; found family remains, and truth proves worth its price.
